title: Townline sync - whitespace reprioritization and exec ask grid (draft)
summary: Working draft for the upcoming company-wide 'townline' sync. Focus: compress open work (whitespace) into a tightened set of priorities, refine the executive asks we present, and sketch comms + rehearsal plan for the all-hands briefing. This doc is intentionally practical and has TODOs, open questions, and a short decision log.
content:
Purpose:

- Short: Get the company aligned on a trimmed set of priorities for the next 6 weeks and surface clear executive asks for resource reallocation or unblockers.
- Longer: We have a lot of ‘whitespace’ — low-confidence projects, half-specified experiments, and deferred maintenance — that are diluting focus. The townline sync will be the mechanism to: (1) call out whitespace, (2) reassign or retire items, and (3) create actionable exec asks (funding, headcount, policy) with owners.

Context & why now:

- Q4 velocity needs: Dedicated and Private launch windows + enterprise sales cycles require a narrower feed of high-impact work.
- Observability: We’re seeing increasing cross-team friction where small infra items block product workstreams.
- People bandwidth: hiring slower than planned; cannot grow parallel initiatives.

Guiding principles for decisions (use in the sync):

1) Impact density: prioritize work that unlocks revenue or reduces >50% ops toil for users.
2) Reversible moves: prefer experiments with clear rollback/fail-fast criteria.
3) Owner clarity: every retained item must have an named owner and a 4-week plan.
4) Surface risks early: any ask that needs >$50k or cross-org approvals must be explicit in the exec ask grid.

Proposed agenda (45 minutes total):

- 0-5m: Framing & ask (CEO/COO) — why we’re tightening scope and the expected outcome of the meeting.
- 5-20m: Whitespace triage (product/ops leads) — 6-8 candidate items called out with one-liner impact and recommended disposition (pause/continue/accelerate).
- 20-30m: Exec ask grid (finance + product) — three asks surfaced, owners, and decision deadlines.
- 30-40m: Risks & fallback plans (SRE/security/legal) — major external dependencies, compliance windows, and mitigations.
- 40-45m: Rapid commitments & next steps — owners commit to a 4-week plan and follow-up cadence.

Whitespace candidates (raw notes - expand before sync):

- API docs refresh project (PD-221) — status: half-done; impact: lowers new-customer onboarding time; ask: 0.2 FE contractor for 6 weeks or deprioritize.
- Internal eval harness for embedding regressions — status: prototype; impact: prevents quality regressions that cost us dollars in re-evals; ask: 1 engineering sprint to productionize.
- Dedicated: burst-capacity pricing experiment — status: scoped, needs billing backend; impact: could increase committed revenue; ask: 2 sprints infra + product.
- Small infra backlog (kv-cache eviction edgecases) — status: SRE backlog; impact: occasional tail-latency spikes; ask: defer unless observed error rate >0.5%.
- Regional compliance gating for APAC partner — status: docs ready; impact: enterprise deal; ask: legal review + KMS integration slot in next two sprints.

Executive ask grid (format = ask | owner | cost/risk | deadline | decision needed):

- Ask 1: Reserve 2 FTE-equivalent contractor-weeks for API docs refresh | Owner: Maya R. | Cost: ~$22k | Deadline: 2024-10-25 | Decision: approve funding or retire project.
- Ask 2: Prioritize embedding eval harness as a sprint in core infra roadmap | Owner: Evan C. | Cost: reassign 1 eng sprint | Deadline: 2024-10-30 | Decision: scheduling & acceptance criteria.
- Ask 3: Legal resource for APAC compliance push (KMS/HSM signoff) | Owner: Liam O'N. | Cost: low cash, medium latency risk | Deadline: 2024-11-07 | Decision: commit legal 0.5 PM-week.

Communications plan (pre, during, post):

- Pre-sync (48h): short pre-read + one-pager sent to staff channel and email with clear ask: we will retire or reassign items; bring objections in the thread.
- During: use slide-lite format — 3 slides: framing, whitespace table (with dispositions highlighted), exec asks (with yes/no options).
- Post-sync (24h): decision digest: list of retained items + owners + 4-week plan + what was retired with rationale. Publish to #townline-summary and Confluence.

Rehearsal checklist (owners labeled):

- Slides & one-pager finalized (Aisha) — TODO: pull metrics for top 3 items, embed 30/60/90 impact estimates.
- Confirm owners can commit to 4-week plans (Leads) — TODO: collect commitments 48h before meeting.
- Legal/Compliance presence confirmed (Liam) — TODO: escalate if >72h notice required.
- Dry run with executive sponsors (CEO + COO) scheduled (Aisha) — try to run 30m run-through 2 days before sync.

Decision log (live during sync):

- [ ] Item: API docs refresh — decision: (pending)
- [ ] Item: Embedding eval harness — decision: (pending)
- [ ] Item: APAC compliance push — decision: (pending)

Open questions / blockers (capture before sync):

- Which customers are we willing to deprioritize to free bandwidth for APAC compliance?
- Is there budget left in the Q4 contingency for contractor support? (Finance: pinged)
- Are there hidden infra dependencies for the embedding eval harness (model-serving contract changes)?

Risks & mitigations (short):

- Risk: Retiring a project that later becomes a customer blocker. Mitigation: 2-week grace where retired items can be flagged for immediate re-evaluation.
- Risk: Exec ask not approved and cross-org morale hit. Mitigation: present two alternatives (funding or reduced scope) and commit to transparent rationale.
- Risk: Legal/Compliance delays push APAC deal beyond quarter. Mitigation: contingency elevator: offer temporary hosted workaround under NDA with limited features.

Action items (owners & deadlines):

- Aisha: finalize slides + metrics (due 2024-10-16).
- Leads: submit 4-week plan templates for retained items (due 2024-10-18).
- Finance: confirm contractor budget availability (due 2024-10-20).
- Legal: validate KMS slot and high-level signoff plan (due 2024-10-21).

Notes to self / working thoughts (rough):

- Keep language non-punitive — we’re pruning to amplify impact, not to punish teams.
- Keep the number of retained items per org <=3. If more, force a rank and one to retire.
- Consider a small 'experiments' bucket for items we want to keep but limit to 2-week micro-OKRs.

Slack/refs: #company-townline, #eng-all-hands, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/42, Confluence: CONFLUENCE-1234.

Appendix (metrics to pull for pre-read):

- New customer onboarding time (median) — last 30 days.
- Token spend per top-10 routes — last 14 days.
- Incidents / P95 latency regressions attributed to kv-cache issues — 30d.
- Demo readiness score for APAC partner — checklist completed items count.

---

Small quick script for the CEO framing (draft):

"We’ve been highly creative this year — lots of initiatives, experiments, and important work. That energy served us well, but we now need to amplify the things that most clearly move revenue and reliability in the near term. This sync is about choosing what we double down on and what we put into a short-term holding pattern. We’ll make concrete decisions (and owners will deliver a 4-week plan). Expect transparency and follow-up."

End of doc — please add edits/objections inline.
